questions.q: By default, when does an action with no custom Configure run after setting execute?
options: Only when the previous action has failed
Only when the previous action is successful
Only when the previous action is skipped
Always, regardless of the previous action's outcome
questions.explain: The default Configure run after condition is "is successful" — an action only runs if the immediately preceding action completed without error.

questions.q: Castlebridge Logistics wants a notification email to fire only when its Dataverse update step breaks or times out, never on success. Which Run After settings should the email step use?
options: Is successful only
Has failed and has timed out, with is successful unchecked
Is skipped only
All four conditions checked at once
questions.explain: Unchecking "is successful" and checking "has failed" and "has timed out" makes the step an error branch that only runs when the prior action breaks or exceeds its timeout.

questions.q: In the scope-based try/catch pattern, how is the "Catch" scope configured to activate?
options: Its Run After is set to trigger when the "Try" scope has failed
It runs automatically after every flow run, regardless of outcome
It is triggered manually by the flow owner
It replaces the "Try" scope entirely once added
questions.explain: The "Catch" scope's Configure run after setting is set to the "Try" scope's "has failed" outcome, so it only executes when something inside Try breaks.

questions.q: What does the result() function return when used inside a Catch scope?
options: A random error code with no detail
The outcome of every action inside the paired Try scope, including which one failed
The name of the flow's owner
A list of all flows in the environment
questions.explain: result() returns the full outcome of every action inside the referenced scope, which lets a Catch block identify exactly which action failed and why.

questions.q: Why would an action's Configure run after setting have both "is successful" and "has failed" checked at the same time?
options: This combination is invalid and Power Automate blocks it
To make the action run regardless of the previous step's outcome, such as a cleanup or logging step
To force the action to fail intentionally
To skip the action entirely
questions.explain: Checking multiple conditions makes the action run in any of the checked outcomes — checking both "is successful" and "has failed" means it runs no matter how the previous step ended, which suits a logging or cleanup step.
